correctness.rationale: The negative-integer polylogarithm identity gives the Eulerian quotient exactly. The low indices \(0,1,2\) are positive discrete Laplace transforms. For every \(i\ge3\), an Eulerian zero in \((-1,0)\) is simple and cannot cancel in the next polynomial by the Eulerian differential recurrence; under \(z=e^{-t}\) it becomes a pole in \(\Re t>0\), impossible for a completely monotone Laplace transform. The logarithmic statements follow from the explicit \(i=1\) logarithmic derivative and the same numerator-zero obstruction for \(i=2\).
